paragraphs.source_en: The authors of the Bubaline engravings and Round Head paintings belonged probably to different cultural groups. The motifs, styles and techniques of the two artistic traditions are completely different and they are also found in different regions. Various ethnic groups may have coexisted in the Central Sahara in the same period, making their rock art in separate territories. The advent of Pastoralism was an event affecting the whole Sahara (Smith 1992). It provoked the migration of people over large distances, so that the new populations who arrived in the Central Sahara found the existing Bubaline engravings and the Round Head paintings. They added their images of domesticated animals next to the already existing rock art but the wild animals also continued to be represented until the historical period.
